study.title: Altered Brain Regional Homogeneity Following Electro-Acupuncture Stimulation at Sanyinjiao (SP6) in Women With Premenstrual Syndrome
study.study_design: within-subject pre-post design; follow-up study using same patient samples as previously published manuscript (Liao et al., 2017); non-repeated event-related (NRER) paradigm
study.population: Twenty-three females with PMS recruited via advertisements posted at Guangxi University of Chinese Medicine
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) 18–45 years old, right-handed; (2) regular menstrual cycle separated by 24–35 days; (3) premenstrual symptoms occurring 2 weeks before menses in most menstrual cycles; (4) symptoms disappear shortly following the onset of menses; (5) symptoms interfere with daily functioning and/or relationships and/or cause emotional or physical distress or suffering; (6) symptoms periodically appear in the late luteal phase of menstrual cycle and relieve soon after the middle-follicular phase; and (7) symptoms do not worsen due to another physical or mental chronic disorder
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) a history of other diseases, including menopausal syndrome, dysmenorrhea, thyroid disease, mastopathy, gynecological inflammation, hysterectomy or bilateral oophorectomy, cancer, or diabetes; (2) a history of psychiatric disorders, such as schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, delusional mental disorder, organic mental disorder, psychotic features coordinated or uncoordinated with mood or bipolar disorder; (3) use of benzodiazepines, steroid compound, or other psychotropic drugs; (4) is lactating or pregnant; (5) has any MRI or acupuncture contraindication; and (6) a history of alcohol or drug abuse or is a smoker

arms.arm_label_exact: PMS patients receiving EAS at SP6
arms.dropouts: Three participants excluded due to obvious head motion

conditions.timepoint_exact: 6–12 min (needle in at 6 min, needle out at 12 min per paradigm figure)
conditions.scan_context: EAS delivered outside scanner per paradigm; resting-state scans acquired before and after

conditions.timepoint_exact: after EAS (time 12–18 min per paradigm figure)

non_acupuncture_locations_exact: a point 1.0 cm away from SP6 (reference electrode insertion point)
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: 3 cun (1 cun = 3.33 cm) directly above the tip of the medial malleoulus on the posterior border of the tibia; left leg
interventions.needle_type_exact: stainless-steel disposable needle (HuaTuo-brand, Suzhou, Jiangsu, China)
interventions.manipulation_exact: EAS executed by inserting needle into SP6; another electrode connected to acupuncture needle superficially inserted into a point 1.0 cm away from SP6
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: Deqi sensations are thought to have therapeutic effects in clinical practice; participants asked to recall Deqi sensations after fMRI scan
interventions.needle_retention_exact: 6 min (needle in at 6 min, needle out at 12 min per NRER paradigm figure)
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: experienced and licensed acupuncturist; device type: HuaTuo-brand, SDZ-V-type, Shanghai, China
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: keep their eyes closed, but to stay awake during the fMRI scan; after fMRI scan, asked to recall Deqi sensations and complete the VAS
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: According to traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), sanyinjiao (SP6) has been shown to ameliorate menstrual-related disorders, including primary dysmenorrhea and PMS; SP6 is commonly selected as the acupoint of choice for improving the physical and psychological symptoms of PMS in clinical settings

sensory_interoceptive_responses.instrument_name_exact: visual analog scale (VAS); includes sensations of soreness, numbness, fullness, heaviness, tingling, coolness, warmth, sharp pain, dull pain, aching and pressure
sensory_interoceptive_responses.reporting_format: mean ± SD (error bar stands for SD as per Figure 2)
sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: Soreness, numbness, fullness, heaviness and tingling were the most commonly reported Deqi sensations (see Figure 2)
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Intensity values reported graphically in Figure 2; exact numeric values not reported in text or table. Figure shows soreness, numbness, fullness, heaviness, tingling as highest intensity; coolness, warmth, sharp pain, dull pain, aching, pressure reported at lower intensity.

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: Magnetom Verio, Siemens Medical, Erlangen, Germany
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: single-shot gradient-recalled echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence; high-resolution T1-weighted structural images collected by a volumetric three-dimensional spoiled gradient recall sequence
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: re-sampled to 3 mm × 3 mm × 3 mm voxels; slice thickness = 5 mm (fMRI); slice thickness = 1 mm (T1)
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 6 min resting-state scan before EAS; 6 min resting-state scan after EAS
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: montreal neurological institute (MNI) space using normalization parameters estimated by T1 structural image unified segmentation
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian kernel of 6 mm full-width at half-maximum
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: If the translation/rotation was more than 1.5 mm/1.5°, the data was discarded
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: temporal filtering (0.01–0.08 Hz); linear drift removed
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: Several sources of spurious variance, such as the estimated motion parameters, average BOLD signals in ventricular and white matter regions, were filtered from the functional images
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: false discovery rate (FDR) corrected, p < 0.05; cluster size >30

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture or healthy control condition was included in the study. Authors explicitly acknowledge this as a limitation: 'the present study only demonstrated increased/decreased ReHo values in the brain of PMS patients modulated by acupuncture at SP6 but did not show that these ReHo values were PMS specific, as there were no healthy controls or sham conditions.'
Expectancy, blinding success, and credibility were not assessed or reported. Study is within-subject pre-post design without sham control, making blinding assessment not applicable.

Exact numeric VAS/Deqi intensity values for all 11 subscales (soreness, numbness, fullness, heaviness, tingling, coolness, warmth, sharp pain, dull pain, aching, pressure) are only available from Figure 2 bar chart and were not reported in text or a numeric table. Exact values could not be extracted reliably from the PDF figure.

Supplementary Table S1 containing correlation analysis between Deqi sensations and ReHo changes in certain brain regions is referenced in the text but was not provided in the PDF. Several Deqi sensations (Coolness, Warmth, Pressure and Sharp pain) were positively correlated with ReHo changes at bilateral precuneus, bilateral insula and left putamen; tingling and numbness were negatively correlated with ReHo changes at precuneus and insula. Full statistical values unavailable without supplement.
Adverse events are not reported or discussed in the paper.
Electrical stimulation parameters for EAS (frequency, intensity/amplitude, waveform) at SP6 are not reported in the methods, only the device brand (HuaTuo-brand, SDZ-V-type) is mentioned.
The needle insertion depth at SP6 is not reported. Penetration depth in mm is not stated.

The NRER paradigm figure (Figure 1B) shows needle in at 6 min and needle out at 12 min, implying 6-min needle retention during EAS. However, two 6-min resting state scans (pre at 0-6 min and post at 12-18 min) were acquired inside the scanner. It is ambiguous whether EAS was administered inside or outside the scanner; the description implies EAS and fMRI were conducted in sequence (fMRI before, EAS, fMRI after) rather than simultaneously.

The paper states this is a follow-up study using the same patient samples as Liao et al. (2017). The pre-EAS resting state scan data may therefore be the same dataset used in the prior publication. This should be noted for systematic review duplicate detection.
PMID is not reported on the PDF. DOI is 10.3389/fnhum.2018.00104.
Table 2 T-values for decreased ReHo regions are reported as negative values (-3.89, -5.16, -5.89, -4.66), consistent with the direction of decrease. These have been preserved as reported.

No information is provided about post-EAS clinical symptom improvement from the single-session EAS. DRSP scores were used for diagnostic characterization only; no pre-post EAS clinical outcome scores are reported.

The study scans were performed 'between 20:00 and 22:00 to ensure a relatively stable and low level of endogenous cortisol and estradiol' and 'during the late luteal phase of the menstrual cycle.' All fMRI results therefore apply specifically to this hormonal phase and time window.
